pathway.title: CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. The existing capital structure is simple and moderately levered. CCC has one senior secured term loan with USD 1,281.2 million of principal at 2026-09-30 and a USD 250.0 million revolver that is undrawn, with USD 249.0 million available after USD 1.0 million of letters of credit [CP-1 debt register]. Gross leverage is 2.64x and net leverage 2.22x on LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 484.9 million, down from 2.96x and 2.71x at FY2025; the fall in net debt of USD 101.5 million over nine months is USD 91.7 million of cash build and USD 9.8 million of scheduled repayment [CP-1 leverage chart data; calculation K5]. (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the reading is Analyst Interpretation.)

2. Headline leverage rests on an earnings measure that adds back share-based pay. LTM Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 126.7 million of share-based compensation and related payroll tax; after deducting it, gross leverage is 3.58x and net 3.01x, and at FY2025 the same sensitivity gave 5.07x gross [CP-1 financials and credit metrics]. The covenant definition that lenders use is not in the pack, so which of the two bases the lenders see is unknown. (Analyst Interpretation; covenant definition is Insufficient Information.)

3. Cash conversion and debt service are strong. LTM free cash flow is USD 311.4 million, 64.2% of Adjusted EBITDA, against USD 13.0 million of annual scheduled amortisation, and LTM Adjusted EBITDA covers cash paid for interest 6.69x (4.95x after the share-based pay deduction) [CP-1; calculations K3 and K1]. Capital spending is light at 5.9% of LTM revenue. (Documentary Fact for inputs; ratios are Analyst Interpretation.)

4. Revenue is recurring and contracted, with named limits. Software subscriptions are 96% of revenue; insurer contracts run about three to five years; remaining performance obligations were USD 1,808 million at 2026-09-30, of which USD 806 million falls within twelve months, against USD 1,891 million at year end; net dollar retention is 108% and gross dollar retention 98% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Total backlog is lower than at year end and renewals are excluded from it, so visibility is twelve-month rather than long-dated. (Documentary Fact.)

5. Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term wall. Cash was USD 202.9 million at 2026-09-30, liquidity including the revolver is USD 451.9 million, and the term loan has USD 3.3 million of remaining 2026 amortisation, USD 13.0 million a year for 2027 to 2031 and a USD 1,212.8 million balloon on 2032-01-23 [CP-1 liquidity and maturity chart data]. The springing leverage test applies only if revolver borrowings reach the threshold, and the revolver was undrawn. (Documentary Fact.)

6. Debt has funded shareholder returns. Term loan principal rose from USD 776.0 million at FY2024 to USD 1,291.0 million at FY2025, with new term loans of USD 525.0 million in 2025: USD 225.0 million alongside the EvolutionIQ acquisition and USD 300.0 million for an accelerated share repurchase [CP-1A governance table; calculation K5]. Leverage rose from 1.95x to 2.96x over FY2025 and has since fallen to 2.64x. No priming, uptiering, drop-down or non-pro-rata transaction appears in the sources read, but the credit agreement that would show the permitted capacity is not in the pack. (Documentary Fact; the willingness reading is Analyst Interpretation.)

7. The take-private is the decisive uncertainty. The merger agreement of 2026-10-14 converts each share to USD 7.75 in cash, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, has no financing condition and carries fees of USD 149.52 million payable by CCC in stated cases and about USD 313.99 million payable by the buyer if it fails to fund [CP-1A transaction summary]. The equity price on the basic share count is about USD 4,581 million, against net debt of USD 1,078.3 million, so the buyer must fund a purchase price several times the existing net debt; how much of it is new debt, how the existing term loan is treated and what covenants follow are Not supplied. (Documentary Fact for the terms; the funding reading is Analyst Interpretation; financing terms are Insufficient Information.)

runs.text: Strengths. First, CCC has recurring, contracted revenue: 96% of revenue is subscription, insurer contracts average about three to five years and the customer base includes 27 of the top 30 automotive insurers, with retention at 108% net and 98% gross (Documentary Fact; CP-1A company and operating model). Second, CCC generates cash against light debt service: free cash flow of USD 311.4 million LTM, cash interest cover of 6.69x and a single term loan with USD 13.0 million of annual amortisation until 2032 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). Third, CCC has ample liquidity: USD 202.9 million of cash and USD 249.0 million of undrawn revolver, with the revolver's springing leverage test untested while undrawn (Documentary Fact; CP-1). Fourth, leverage has been trending down: gross leverage has fallen from 2.96x at FY2025 to 2.64x at LTM Q3 2026 while cash built by USD 91.7 million (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1).

Weaknesses. First, earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 126.7 million of share-based pay and related payroll tax over the LTM period, and the lender definition is unknown, so gross leverage is 2.64x on the headline base and 3.58x on the stricter base (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1). Second, capital allocation: debt-funded repurchases of USD 300.0 million in December 2025 and repurchases from the principal equity owner in 2023 and 2025 show a willingness to return capital using the balance sheet (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance table). Third, customer power and concentration: no customer exceeded 10% of FY2025 revenue, but the filing states a relatively small number of customers account for a significant portion of revenue, large customers have bargaining power and the company has had to cut average selling prices before; customer-level data is Not supplied (Insufficient Information on size; CP-1A). Fourth, floating-rate exposure: USD 531.2 million of the term loan is unhedged and the USD 750.0 million of swaps at about 3.94% expire on 2027-07-31, so a 100 basis point rise adds about USD 5.3 million of annual interest now and about USD 12.8 million after the swaps expire (Analyst Interpretation; calculation K2). Fifth, asset base: goodwill and intangible assets are USD 2,897.6 million, 80.4% of total assets, and tangible equity is negative USD 1,055.7 million, so asset coverage for creditors depends on the franchise and not on tangible assets; this is a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion (Analyst Interpretation; calculation K4). Sixth, change of control: the take-private leaves the post-closing leverage, ranking of the existing loan, covenants and sponsor behaviour Insufficient Information, and sponsor behaviour must not be inferred from the buyer's identity (Insufficient Information; CP-1A).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transaction is a pending acquisition of the whole company. On 2026-10-14 the company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Mozart Parent, LLC and Mozart Merger Sub (DE), Inc.; the merger sub merges into the company, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (10-Q Q3 page:29). Each outstanding share other than certain excluded shares converts into the right to receive 7.75 US dollars in cash; the board approved it with all directors present voting in favour and resolved to recommend it (10-Q Q3 page:29). The company's release, dated 2026-10-29, says the buyer is a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management, that the all-cash deal represents an enterprise value of approximately 6.1 billion US dollars, that guidance is suspended and that no earnings call will be held (release page:2); these are management statements, and neither GTCR nor Elliott is named in the sections of the 10-Q that were read (searched for both names in the 10-Q Q3 text). Status: signed, not closed. Closing is subject to customary conditions including adoption by holders of a majority of the outstanding shares, expiry or termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period and the absence of a prohibiting law or order; the merger is not subject to a financing condition and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, after which the shares are delisted (10-Q Q3 page:30). Either side may terminate if the merger is not consummated on or before 2027-04-14, among other rights (10-Q Q3 page:51). The company must pay Parent a fee of 149.52 million if the agreement ends in specified cases such as a superior proposal, and Parent would owe the company approximately 313.99 million if it fails to fund the equity financing or close the debt or preferred equity financing the agreement contemplates (10-Q Q3 page:51). The agreement restricts, without Parent's consent, incurring certain debt, paying dividends, repurchasing stock, settling certain legal proceedings and some capital expenditure (10-Q Q3 pages:22, 45, 52), and stockholder complaints about the merger are a disclosed risk (10-Q Q3 page:53).

New debt issues: no new debt was raised in 2026 to date (10-Q Q3 page:45, "We did not incur any new borrowings in 2026"). The merger agreement contemplates "debt or preferred equity financing" for the buyer (10-Q Q3 page:51), but the amounts, instruments, ranking, security and the issuer of that financing are Not supplied, as is the treatment of the existing 2021 Credit Agreement term loan and revolver at closing (repaid, assumed or amended). Use of proceeds is not stated in the pack; the merger consideration is payable to stockholders (10-Q Q3 page:29). The liquidity effects disclosed are the fee exposures above and the restrictions on the company's use of cash. Arithmetic on stated figures (calculation T1): 591,041,172 shares at 7.75 US dollars is about 4,581 million US dollars on the basic share count, to which net debt of 1,078 million at 2026-09-30 adds about 5,659 million; the release's approximately 6.1 billion US dollars is about 441 million higher, and the pack does not bridge the difference (dilutive securities, transaction costs and other items are not itemised). The enterprise value is about 12.6 times LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 484,946 thousand, an arithmetic ratio on management's approximate figure and not a valuation conclusion. The filings also describe 8,625,000 Sponsor Vesting Shares and 15.0 million Company Earnout Shares whose release depends on a share price threshold or a change in control "as defined in the Business Combination Agreement" (10-K page:165); that agreement is not in the pack, so whether the merger is such a change in control is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: View: the financial base is sufficient and consistent for a bounded credit snapshot, with the restrictions listed below. Every statement figure used here is taken from a filed statement or note; the three discrete 2026 quarters are the reported three-month columns, FY2025 and FY2024 are audited, and LTM Q3 2026 is calculated as FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025 (calculation C1). The reported statements reconcile: revenue, operating cash flow, free cash flow and Adjusted EBITDA for the quarters add to the nine-month columns within a difference of at most 2 thousand (C9), and the term loan carrying amount ties to its components. The capital structure is one senior secured term loan with 1,281,216 principal at 2026-09-30 and an undrawn 250.0 million revolver; the only other funded obligation is a 27,562 promissory note issued by CCC Cayman, the parent of the China subsidiaries, without recourse to the registrant. The strongest contrary points are these. First, headline leverage is built on Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back share-based compensation and related payroll tax of 126,687 over the LTM period; on the lower base gross leverage is 3.58x, not 2.64x. Second, the lender covenant is a springing leverage test that applies only when revolver borrowings reach the 35% threshold (the filings word it as "a minimum of 35.0%" in 10-K page:81 and as exceeding 35% of commitments in 10-K page:161), and its ratio definition is not in the pack, so headroom is Not calculable. Third, the merger agreed on 2026-10-14 is a subsequent event; the existing term loan may be repaid or kept at closing, and the pack does not say which, so any forward leverage is Not calculable. What can proceed: reported-fact summaries, LTM and discrete-quarter metrics, liquidity and maturity profile, and the leverage and cover ratios as issuer-basis measures. What is restricted: covenant compliance or headroom, pro forma capital structure, and any Q4 2025 discrete figure not derived by difference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: View: the business facts are well documented and the transaction facts are documented only at summary level. CCC is a US software-as-a-service and AI platform for the auto insurance and collision repair economy; 96% of revenue is software subscriptions on multi-year contracts, the customer base is broad but includes a few very large insurers, and there is a documented history of financing acquisitions and shareholder returns with debt. The transaction is a pending merger signed on 2026-10-14, a subsequent event to the Q3 2026 period: each share converts to 7.75 US dollars in cash and the company becomes a privately held wholly owned subsidiary of Mozart Parent, LLC, while the release separately attributes the acquisition to a consortium led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management; the filings do not state how that consortium relates to Parent. The strongest contrary evidence for a stable creditor view is that everything that governs the creditor after closing is outside the pack: the executed merger agreement, the debt and preferred equity financing it contemplates, and any change-of-control terms in the 2021 Credit Agreement. The ownership picture before the deal is also thin: the filings name a "principal equity owner" without naming it or giving a holding. The mechanism that matters is a change of control that is documented as to price and timing but not as to leverage: the equity purchase price at the offer price is far larger than the existing net debt, and the split between new debt, preferred equity and equity is Not supplied. What can proceed: business risk assessment, revenue durability, concentration and cash conversion analysis, and a documented capital-allocation history. What is restricted: any statement about sponsor behaviour after closing, willingness to support, post-deal leverage, or the fate of the existing term loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction is a pending acquisition of the whole company. On 2026-10-14 the company entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Mozart Parent, LLC and Mozart Merger Sub (DE), Inc.; the merger sub merges into the company, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (10-Q Q3 page:29). Each outstanding share other than certain excluded shares converts into the right to receive 7.75 US dollars in cash; the board approved it with all directors present voting in favour and resolved to recommend it (10-Q Q3 page:29). The company's release, dated 2026-10-29, says the buyer is a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management, that the all-cash deal represents an enterprise value of approximately 6.1 billion US dollars, that guidance is suspended and that no earnings call will be held (release page:2); these are management statements, and neither GTCR nor Elliott is named in the sections of the 10-Q that were read (searched for both names in the 10-Q Q3 text). Status: signed, not closed. Closing is subject to customary conditions including adoption by holders of a majority of the outstanding shares, expiry or termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period and the absence of a prohibiting law or order; the merger is not subject to a financing condition and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, after which the shares are delisted (10-Q Q3 page:30). Either side may terminate if the merger is not consummated on or before 2027-04-14, among other rights (10-Q Q3 page:51). The company must pay Parent a fee of 149.52 million if the agreement ends in specified cases such as a superior proposal, and Parent would owe the company approximately 313.99 million if it fails to fund the equity financing or close the debt or preferred equity financing the agreement contemplates (10-Q Q3 page:51). The agreement restricts, without Parent's consent, incurring certain debt, paying dividends, repurchasing stock, settling certain legal proceedings and some capital expenditure (10-Q Q3 pages:22, 45, 52), and stockholder complaints about the merger are a disclosed risk (10-Q Q3 page:53).

fields.value: This is the fundamental credit synthesis for CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. (CCC) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, built only from the settled CP-0, CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs. It covers business risk, financial risk and liquidity at the current period (Q3 2026, LTM to 2026-09-30) against FY2025, in USD, and it makes no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.value: CP-2 reads upstream registers only and quotes no source text. The issuer sources below underlie the CP-1 and CP-1A figures and facts it cites; they were not re-read for this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CCC Intelligent Solutions Holdings Inc. has a sound standalone credit profile today, but the pending take-private makes its post-closing credit unassessable. The strongest support is recurring subscription revenue at 96% of the total, leverage of 2.64x gross and 2.22x net on LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 484.9 million, free cash flow of USD 311.4 million and liquidity of USD 451.9 million against a single term loan due in 2032. The weakest point is that headline EBITDA adds back USD 126.7 million of share-based pay, so gross leverage is 3.58x once it is deducted, and that debt has funded shareholder returns. What decides the outcome is whether the existing term loan stays in place or is replaced by new buyer financing, which the pack does not disclose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CCC is a cash-generative subscription software borrower whose moderate, mostly term-debt leverage and ample liquidity support its existing 2032 term loan, but whose headline earnings flatter leverage and whose creditor position will be reset by the take-private on terms the pack does not show. (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 leverage and liquidity figures, CP-1A transaction and governance rows.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The existing capital structure is simple and moderately levered. CCC has one senior secured term loan with USD 1,281.2 million of principal at 2026-09-30 and a USD 250.0 million revolver that is undrawn, with USD 249.0 million available after USD 1.0 million of letters of credit [CP-1 debt register]. Gross leverage is 2.64x and net leverage 2.22x on LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 484.9 million, down from 2.96x and 2.71x at FY2025; the fall in net debt of USD 101.5 million over nine months is USD 91.7 million of cash build and USD 9.8 million of scheduled repayment [CP-1 leverage chart data; calculation K5]. (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the reading is Analyst Interpretation.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Headline leverage rests on an earnings measure that adds back share-based pay. LTM Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 126.7 million of share-based compensation and related payroll tax; after deducting it, gross leverage is 3.58x and net 3.01x, and at FY2025 the same sensitivity gave 5.07x gross [CP-1 financials and credit metrics]. The covenant definition that lenders use is not in the pack, so which of the two bases the lenders see is unknown. (Analyst Interpretation; covenant definition is Insufficient Information.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Cash conversion and debt service are strong. LTM free cash flow is USD 311.4 million, 64.2% of Adjusted EBITDA, against USD 13.0 million of annual scheduled amortisation, and LTM Adjusted EBITDA covers cash paid for interest 6.69x (4.95x after the share-based pay deduction) [CP-1; calculations K3 and K1]. Capital spending is light at 5.9% of LTM revenue. (Documentary Fact for inputs; ratios are Analyst Interpretation.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Revenue is recurring and contracted, with named limits. Software subscriptions are 96% of revenue; insurer contracts run about three to five years; remaining performance obligations were USD 1,808 million at 2026-09-30, of which USD 806 million falls within twelve months, against USD 1,891 million at year end; net dollar retention is 108% and gross dollar retention 98% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Total backlog is lower than at year end and renewals are excluded from it, so visibility is twelve-month rather than long-dated. (Documentary Fact.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term wall. Cash was USD 202.9 million at 2026-09-30, liquidity including the revolver is USD 451.9 million, and the term loan has USD 3.3 million of remaining 2026 amortisation, USD 13.0 million a year for 2027 to 2031 and a USD 1,212.8 million balloon on 2032-01-23 [CP-1 liquidity and maturity chart data]. The springing leverage test applies only if revolver borrowings reach the threshold, and the revolver was undrawn. (Documentary Fact.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Debt has funded shareholder returns. Term loan principal rose from USD 776.0 million at FY2024 to USD 1,291.0 million at FY2025, with new term loans of USD 525.0 million in 2025: USD 225.0 million alongside the EvolutionIQ acquisition and USD 300.0 million for an accelerated share repurchase [CP-1A governance table; calculation K5]. Leverage rose from 1.95x to 2.96x over FY2025 and has since fallen to 2.64x. No priming, uptiering, drop-down or non-pro-rata transaction appears in the sources read, but the credit agreement that would show the permitted capacity is not in the pack. (Documentary Fact; the willingness reading is Analyst Interpretation.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. The take-private is the decisive uncertainty. The merger agreement of 2026-10-14 converts each share to USD 7.75 in cash, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, has no financing condition and carries fees of USD 149.52 million payable by CCC in stated cases and about USD 313.99 million payable by the buyer if it fails to fund [CP-1A transaction summary]. The equity price on the basic share count is about USD 4,581 million, against net debt of USD 1,078.3 million, so the buyer must fund a purchase price several times the existing net debt; how much of it is new debt, how the existing term loan is treated and what covenants follow are Not supplied. (Documentary Fact for the terms; the funding reading is Analyst Interpretation; financing terms are Insufficient Information.)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, CCC has recurring, contracted revenue: 96% of revenue is subscription, insurer contracts average about three to five years and the customer base includes 27 of the top 30 automotive insurers, with retention at 108% net and 98% gross (Documentary Fact; CP-1A company and operating model). Second, CCC generates cash against light debt service: free cash flow of USD 311.4 million LTM, cash interest cover of 6.69x and a single term loan with USD 13.0 million of annual amortisation until 2032 (Documentary Fact; CP-1). Third, CCC has ample liquidity: USD 202.9 million of cash and USD 249.0 million of undrawn revolver, with the revolver's springing leverage test untested while undrawn (Documentary Fact; CP-1). Fourth, leverage has been trending down: gross leverage has fallen from 2.96x at FY2025 to 2.64x at LTM Q3 2026 while cash built by USD 91.7 million (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 126.7 million of share-based pay and related payroll tax over the LTM period, and the lender definition is unknown, so gross leverage is 2.64x on the headline base and 3.58x on the stricter base (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1). Second, capital allocation: debt-funded repurchases of USD 300.0 million in December 2025 and repurchases from the principal equity owner in 2023 and 2025 show a willingness to return capital using the balance sheet (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance table). Third, customer power and concentration: no customer exceeded 10% of FY2025 revenue, but the filing states a relatively small number of customers account for a significant portion of revenue, large customers have bargaining power and the company has had to cut average selling prices before; customer-level data is Not supplied (Insufficient Information on size; CP-1A). Fourth, floating-rate exposure: USD 531.2 million of the term loan is unhedged and the USD 750.0 million of swaps at about 3.94% expire on 2027-07-31, so a 100 basis point rise adds about USD 5.3 million of annual interest now and about USD 12.8 million after the swaps expire (Analyst Interpretation; calculation K2). Fifth, asset base: goodwill and intangible assets are USD 2,897.6 million, 80.4% of total assets, and tangible equity is negative USD 1,055.7 million, so asset coverage for creditors depends on the franchise and not on tangible assets; this is a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion (Analyst Interpretation; calculation K4). Sixth, change of control: the take-private leaves the post-closing leverage, ranking of the existing loan, covenants and sponsor behaviour Insufficient Information, and sponsor behaviour must not be inferred from the buyer's identity (Insufficient Information; CP-1A).
